{"sample_id": "blind-003f4aa2b681449aa9df4023cbe48356", "theorem": "Let \( N \) be a positive integer. Two persons play the following game. The first player writes a list of positive integers not greater than \( 25 \), not necessarily different, such that their sum is at least \( 200 \). The second player wins if he can select some of these numbers so that their sum \( S \) satisfies the condition \( 200-N \leq S \leq 200+N \). What is the smallest value of \( N \) for which the second player has a winning strategy?", "assumptions": [], "domain": "baltic_mo", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "The smallest value is \(\boxed{11}\).

To prove necessity, let the first player write five \(23\)'s and four \(24\)'s. Their total is
\[
5\cdot23+4\cdot24=211.
\]
Every proper subset has sum at most \(211-23=188\), while the whole list has sum \(211\). Thus no subset sum lies in \([190,210]\), so \(N=10\) (and hence every smaller \(N\)) is insufficient.

Now prove that \(N=11\) always suffices. From the given list choose an inclusion-minimal sublist whose sum \(T\) is at least \(200\). Since every entry is at most \(25\), minimality gives \(T\le224\).

If \(200\le T\le211\), this sublist itself has sum in \([189,211]\).

Suppose \(212\le T\le224\), and write \(T=200+d\), where \(12\le d\le24\). By minimality, removing any entry \(a\) makes the sum less than \(200\); hence
\[
a>T-200=d.
\]
We seek an entry satisfying
\[
d-11\le a\le d+11,
\]
because then
\[
189=T-(d+11)\le T-a\le T-(d-11)=211.
\]
If \(d\ge14\), every entry works: \(a>d\ge d-11\) and \(a\le25\le d+11\).

If \(d=13\), then \(T=213\). Some entry is at most \(24=d+11\), since otherwise all entries would equal \(25\), making \(T\) divisible by \(25\), which \(213\) is not.

If \(d=12\), then \(T=212\). Some entry is at most \(23=d+11\): otherwise all entries would be at least \(24\); at most eight entries would total at most \(200\), while at least nine would total at least \(216\), both impossible.

Thus in every case, deleting a suitable entry from the minimal sublist produces a subset sum in \([189,211]\). Therefore \(N=11\) is sufficient and is the smallest possible value."}
